Theme

Playground equipment, sandbox toys, vehicles and play

racket noun

for tennis or badminton

also racquet, tennis racket, badminton racket

Renaissance

M-O s.v. tennis terms: racquet (Erasmus; Vives 1540)
Traupman 45, 50
Andresian p. 18

rēticulum, rēticulī n.

noun, second declension

Classically a little net or a net bag; Ovid has one in a ball game (Ars 3.361). Erasmus and Vives use it for the strung racket, and so does every modern list.

Other words

  • rēticulum manubriātum — racket with a handle

    also used · modern · Traupman 45, 50

    Traupman’s fuller form; manubriātus “with a handle” is in Lewis & Short.

Examples

  • Quōmodo ergō percutiunt pilam? pugnō, ut follēs? — Nē sīc quidem, sed rēticulō.

    How do they hit the ball, then? With their fist, like footballs? — Not that either: with a racket.Vīv. Exerc. 22

  • In sphaeristēriō lūditur pilā, quam alter mittit, alter excipit, et remittit rēticulō.

    In the ball court they play with a ball, which one throws and the other catches and sends back with a racket.Comen. OP 133

See also tennis, tennis ball, badminton, table tennis.
